title: Understand Ratios
objective: I can write and describe a ratio that compares two quantities.
model: tape diagram and double number line showing 'for every' parts (and counters that build batches)

widgets.component: 5 + 3 tangs, 6 × 3 fragments, divide 6 and 9 by 3, 'times as many'
widgets.root: Checked 8, 18, (2,3), 3: addition for the whole, multiplication, a common factor and multiplicative comparison are the lesson's prerequisites.

widgets.component: write part-to-part and part-to-whole ratios in order
widgets.root: Recomputed 4:1, bananas to total 2:8, boys to girls 12:18 (30 − 18 = 12), dogs to cats 5:9; distractors are the reversed and part-to-whole slips.

widgets.component: reversed order 8:5; part-to-part used for part-to-whole 6:9
widgets.root: The flagged step is the first wrong one in both (write the ratio); fixes 5:8 and 6:15.

widgets.component: pineapple to melon 3:5; trucks to all vehicles 6:16
widgets.root: Recomputed from 5 melon, 3 pineapple, 2 grapes and 10 cars, 6 trucks.

widgets.where: Practice §3 item 3.2 (tbl, word / colon / fraction form)
widgets.root: The cell grader compares only the leading number (value() in assets/studio/kinds-basic.js takes the digits up to the first non-digit), so '9' typed for '9 to 15', '9 to 99' for '9 to 15' and '9:99' for '9:15' are all accepted: the student can pass without writing the second term. The same table cannot tell a correct ratio from a wrong one.
widgets.replacement: Split each form into two numeric boxes (first term, second term) around fixed text: [__] to [__], [__] : [__] and [__]/[__]; grade each box as a number. Keep the three rows (4 cats to 7 dogs shown, 9 red out of 15, 5 wins to 3 losses).

widgets.component: ratio of two groups; part to whole; given a part-to-part ratio find part to whole, with tape diagram
widgets.root: Scanned 300 seeds per level: a 'simplest form' item offers the unsimplified ratio only as a labelled distractor, otherwise no equivalent choice; the tape diagram is drawn from the same numbers as the stem.

widgets.component: add whole batches of a coloured/shaped counter mix to hit a target
widgets.root: Manipulable model for 'for every a there are b' (counters carry colour, shape and letter), with a live ratio table and proportion bar that show structure without the answer.

widgets.where: Practice §5 items 5.1-5.6 (mc, mc, mc, mc, num, mc)
widgets.component: 3:2 dishes scaled to 10 sides; kind of ratio; mains to total; raisins to total; whole of 7 + 3; 20:30 in simplest form
widgets.root: Checked: 15, part-to-part, 3 to 5, 5:13, 10, 2:3. Scaling a ratio with tape diagram and double number line is the lesson's own youDo, and 'simplest form' is in its vocabulary; every stem contains its data.

widgets.component: part-to-whole; whole from part-to-part; tape diagram with a total (4:9, 91 total → 28)
widgets.root: L4 tape drawn to scale from the ratio; 91 ÷ 13 × 4 = 28 checked.

widgets.component: wrong total 8 for 12; order of urchins to sea stars; part-to-whole; simplifying 12:18 by subtraction
widgets.root: Flagged steps are the first wrong ones; fixes 4:12, 7:4, 6:15, 2:3.

widgets.component: write three different ratios from a bag of marbles; invent a story with two ratios

widgets.where: Challenge §2 items 2.3, 2.4, 2.6 (mc bar chart, num, mc)
widgets.component: gobies to all fish from a bar chart (3:18 = 1:6); 40 fragments in ratio 5:3; turtles and rays
widgets.root: Bar values 9, 6, 3 give gobies to all fish 3:18 = 1:6; 5:3 on 40 gives 25.

widgets.component: complete a ratio table of equivalent ratios
widgets.root: A ratio table filled by a constant multiplier is the representation and the method of 3-3 (Determine Equivalent Ratios Using Tables); 3-1's models are the tape diagram and the double number line and its vocabulary has no ratio table.
widgets.replacement: Replace with a tape-diagram completion: tape viz {rows:[{label:'Clownfish',parts:[2],groups:5},{label:'Shrimp',parts:[3],groups:5}]} and the questions 'How many shrimp are fed with 10 clownfish?' (15) and 'How many parts of the tape does one tank use in all?' (5).

widgets.component: build the recipe; L4 recover one batch in simplest form from the final mix
widgets.root: Manipulable counters; L4 asks the reverse (12 and 15 → 4:5 per batch), which traps the 'use the final amounts as one batch' misconception.

widgets.component: reef sentences to ratios in simplest form

widgets.root: Only Mia is right: a ratio compares two quantities and is not a single number.

widgets.where: Challenge §5 items 5.1-5.5 (mc, num, mc, num, mc)
widgets.component: 14:21 equivalent to 2:3; 36 fish at 1:4 gives 9; blue to all 3:8; divers 3:2 with 12 gives 8; 12 fish with 4 damselfish
widgets.root: Recomputed 2:3, 9, 3:8, 8, '1 damselfish for every 2 other fish'.
